messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert: serving-runtime eu-west pool experiencing rapid pod crashloops and CUDA OOMs (>25% replicas). Paging oncall-eng.

oncall-eng: Acknowledged. @runtime-eng @infra-oncall please join. Starting triage. Any customer-facing symptoms?

support-ops: Multiple customers seeing 5xxs; our dashboard shows a spike from baseline 0.5% -> 15% on eu-west prod. Filing list of impacted accounts to PMs.

sre-lead: Creating incident ticket INCIDENT-1932109876. Live doc link in channel. We need immediate mitigations to stop autoscaler thrash.

runtime-eng: Root logs show recurring allocation failures: 'GPU OOM: out of memory while allocating 6.4GB for KV cache' then process receives SIGKILL (exit 137). Also seeing NVML reports of fragmentation; some nodes report 95% GPU mem used by rogue processes.

charlie: Ran `nvidia-smi pmon -c 1` on an affected node: a short-lived model init process shows up with high GPU mem then disappears. Probably the runtime tries to reserve full KV then crashes.

infra-oncall: Observed pattern: cluster-autoscaler scales up rapidly when queue depth spikes -> new nodes provision -> kube-scheduler spreads pods -> pods ramp up and try to allocate full KV -> OOM/crash -> eviction -> autoscaler interprets low utilization and scales down -> repeat. This oscillation is triggering crashloops and 'brownouts' where capacity briefly exists but can't serve.

oncall-eng: Initial mitigations proposed: 1) pause cluster-autoscaler scale-ups, 2) set a conservative min-nodes to hold capacity, 3) reduce KV cache limits and disable eager preallocation in runtime, 4) enable fallback routing to quantized model variants and/or route to other regions. I'll enact 1-3 now.

runtime-eng: Pushing a runtime env update to set KV_PREALLOC=false and KV_MAX_MB=384 for the eu-west deployment, and set BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=1024 -> BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=256 to reduce peak memory. Command: `kubectl -n serving set env deployment/runtime KV_PREALLOC=false KV_MAX_MB=384 BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=256 --selector=pool=eu-west`. Rolling update in flight.

infra-oncall: Pausing cluster-autoscaler via annotation and setting min nodes: `kubectl -n kube-system annotate configmap cluster-autoscaler pause=true` and patched minSize for eu-west to 10. Also increased scaleDownDelay to 15m.

product-ops: Heads up: fallback to quantized-small will change model outputs slightly. Preparing message to affected enterprise customers explaining mitigation and ETA.

support-ops: Sent interim status to impacted customers, including workaround to route to alternative region if they want lower latency variance.

dana: Running `kubectl get pods -n serving -l pool=eu-west -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].state}'` shows a lot of 'lastState: terminated reason: OOMKilled'.

charlie: Also noticed some nodes had leftover processes holding GPU memory after pod termination (zombie process). I've restarted docker on those nodes to clear GPU allocations. Command: `systemctl restart nvidia-docker` (done on 3 nodes).

runtime-eng: Enabling routing policy: `PATCH /api/v1/routing/regions/eu-west` set fallback_policy=quantized-small, spillover_regions=[eu-north,us-west]. Applied. Traffic shift started at 10%.

oncall-eng: Monitoring metrics: after KV caps + fallback routing + autoscaler pause, 5xx dropped from 15% -> 4% within 8 minutes. Latency 95p improved; 99p still elevated.

infra-oncall: To prevent further thrash, also applied node taint to newly created nodes so only pods with lower KV settings are scheduled: `kubectl taint nodes <new-node-ids> autoscale-hold=true:NoSchedule`.

sre-lead: Good. Keep autoscaler paused until we validate stability and run an engineered scale test. We'll also run a canary load to ensure nodes handle steady-state.

charlie: Noted one recurring cause: some pods still use older image tag with KV_PREALLOC=true. We're forcing a redeploy to ensure all pods pick up new env. `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime -n serving --selector=pool=eu-west`.

incident-bot: Redeploy triggered by charlie. Monitoring rollout.

support-ops: Current customer impact summary: ~6 enterprise customers saw degraded results; two opened SEV tickets. We've posted a support status update.

product-ops: If we keep quantized fallback in place long-term, need to update docs/contract notes. For now communicate quality tradeoff clearly.

runtime-eng: Observed remaining OOMs are rare and tied to a single old node that didn't restart GPU services correctly. Rebooted node and garbage-collected stale Docker runtimes. OOMs stopped on that node.

oncall-eng: Metrics steady for 20+ minutes. 5xx now ~2.1%. Keeping autoscaler paused and min nodes enforced. Next steps for handoff: infra-oncall will watch overnight, runtime-eng will own postmortem, sre-lead will lead RCA and config change plan.

infra-oncall: Taking watch. Logging runbook steps: unpause autoscaler only after controlled canary scale test and ensuring KV caps removed gradually. Plan to run load test tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

sre-lead: Filing follow-up ticket INCIDENT-1932109876-RCA. Action items: 1) make autoscaler thresholds more conservative for bursty workloads, 2) add guard rails to runtime to detect memory fragmentation and fall back earlier, 3) improve preflight on autoscaler+runtime config rollouts. Owners assigned.

charlie: For completeness, capturing commands used during mitigation in incident doc (autoscaler patch, taint, env set, redeploy, restart nvidia runtime).

incident-bot: Incident status=stabilized; handoff to infra-oncall at 11:45 UTC. Please attach logs and timeline to INCIDENT-1932109876. If errors climb above 5% reopen paging.

oncall-eng: Closing this coordination thread. Thanks team. If any regressions overnight ping infra-oncall and me will respond. :white_check_mark:

support-ops: Final note: customers updated, follow-up scheduled after RCA with suggested SLO changes and a compensating credit if SLA breached.

incident-bot: End of thread.
